record.original_question: Which 2-periodic functions φ on (0, ∞) have the property that the linear span of {φ(nx) : n ≥ 1} is dense in L^2(0, 1)?

evidence.quote: The PDCP asks which 2-periodic functions φ on (0, ∞) have the property that span{φ(nx) : n ≥ 1} is dense in L2(0, 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let φ : (0, ∞) → ℂ be a 2-periodic function whose restriction to (0,1) lies in L²(0,1) (equivalently, identify φ with an odd or general 2-periodic extension of a function in L²(0,1)). For each integer n ≥ 1, let φ_n(x) = φ(nx) for x ∈ (0,1). Characterize all such 2-periodic functions φ for which the linear span of the dilation system {φ_n : n ≥ 1} is dense in L²(0,1).
artifact.status_search_result: The Periodic Dilation Completeness Problem (also known as the Beurling–Wintner problem) is a longstanding open problem in harmonic analysis. Via Beurling's idea and the Bohr transform, it is equivalent to characterizing cyclic vectors for coordinate multiplication operators in the Hardy space H² over the infinite-dimensional polydisk. While substantial partial results exist (e.g., for characteristic functions and various special classes), and connections to questions like the twin prime conjecture are known, no full characterization is available, and the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Periodic Dilation Completeness Problem: Cyclic vectors in the Hardy space over the infinite-dimensional polydisk
status_evidence.snippet: The classical completeness problem raised by Beurling and Wintner... is nowadays commonly called the Periodic Dilation Completeness Problem (PDCP).
status_evidence.claim: PDCP is a classical longstanding problem; partial characterizations via cyclic vectors in H² of the infinite polydisk.

status_evidence.title: The Beurling-Wintner problem for characteristic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Beurling-Wintner problem... related to the Twin Prime Conjecture and the Sophie Germain Prime Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is related to deep number-theoretic conjectures, indicating it is generally open.
